metadata.case_name: LO SIU WA v. NUOVO DESIGN LTD

injuries.description: right 2nd and 3rd fingers: comminuted intra-articular fracture in PIPJ requiring fusion (arthrodesis), cut extensor tendon and cut dorsal branches of digital nerves resulting in shortening of the fingers, stiffness of DIPJ, a fused PIPJ and residue numbness in the fingers distal to laceration;
source: (a) right 2nd and 3rd fingers: comminuted intra-articular fracture in PIPJ requiring fusion (arthrodesis), cut extensor tendon and cut dorsal branches of digital nerves resulting in shortening of the fingers, stiffness of DIPJ, a fused PIPJ and residue numbness in the fingers distal to laceration;
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple sites of hand

injuries.description: right 5th finger: fracture in middle phalanx fixed with K wires, cut extensor tendon and possibly damage nail plate resulting in residual shortening of the finger, residual stiffness of DIPJ and damage nail plate requiring a second operation in December 2007.
source: (c) right 5th finger: fracture in middle phalanx fixed with K wires, cut extensor tendon and possibly damage nail plate resulting in residual shortening of the finger, residual stiffness of DIPJ and damage nail plate requiring a second operation in December 2007.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple sites of hand

injuries.description: scars over the dorsum of the right 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th fingers (combination scars caused by the Accident and surgery) with shortening of right 2nd, 3rd and 5th fingers and loss of most of right 5th nail plate;
source: There were a number of scars over the dorsum of his right 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th fingers, which were combination scars caused by the Accident and surgery.
The right 2nd, 3rd and 5th fingers were shortened by 1cm, 1.5cm and 2mm respectively.
Only about 1/10 of the nail plate of the right 5th finger remained.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple sites of hand

injuries.description: Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Moderate Severity under DSM-IV (psychiatric injury) with persistent symptoms and functional impairment;
source: Dr Chen opined that the plaintiff’s complaints caused by the Accident were compatible with Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Moderate Severity under DSM-IV.

manifestations.description: could not make a power grip with his right hand
residue numbness in the fingers distal to laceration (right 2nd and 3rd fingers)
pain in his right 5th finger terminal phalanx
residual stiffness of DIPJ of right 5th finger
scars over the dorsum of his right 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th fingers
weakness in handgrip (power grip of the right and left hands were 28Kg/f and 50kg/f respectively)
inability to return to pre-Accident work as a master carpenter
difficulty with activities of daily living (eg inability to pick up small objects, wring dry a towel, pour tea, grasp chopsticks or pen)
loss of ability to play billiard which he enjoyed
depressed mood, poor sleep, poor appetite, lack of motivation and interest, low energy, low frustration tolerance, irritability, poor concentration and memory, occasional suicidal ideation

treatments_received: Open reduction, debridement, tendon repair, internal fixation and fusion of the proximal interphalangeal joints (PIPJ) of the right 2nd and 3rd fingers (20 March 2007)
Physiotherapy (initial assessment 9 May 2007; attended for 8 months; discharged 24 December 2007)
Occupational therapy (referred 14 May 2007; attended 25 May to 5 December 2007)
Minor procedure to remove remnant nail under local anaesthesia (admitted 17 December 2007, discharged 19 December 2007)
Psychiatric treatment and counselling at West Kowloon Psychiatric Centre (first seen 16 October 2008); pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy; clinical psychologist assessment (12 March 2010)
treatments_future: Psychiatric and psychological treatment in private sector for at least 1-2 more years with more intensive sessions initially (eg weekly then fortnightly then monthly)

losses.description: Permanent structural impairment of right 2nd and 3rd fingers including fused PIPJ, shortening, stiffness and numbness affecting hand function
Scars over the dorsum of right 2nd-5th fingers and shortening and deformity of right 2nd, 3rd and 5th fingers with loss of most of right 5th nail plate

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty with ADL eg inability to pick up small objects, wring dry a towel, pour tea, grasp chopsticks or pen

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to play billiard which he enjoyed and played once a week before the Accident
Can no longer return to his pre-Accident work as a master carpenter
Marital strain: frequent conflict with his wife, wife mentioned divorce and ran away from home several times; diminished social/leisure activities with wife
